This is a focused regression child of the shipped feature.
GH-665: schema migrations need derived idempotency keys and structured recovery

Make SDK schema-evolution planning ergonomic and deterministic when callers omit a migration id, allow side-effect-free dry-run planning, and route invalid migration input through the standard typed CLI recovery envelope.

Public SDK accepts an optional migration id and derives a deterministic workspace-and-operation-bound key; explicit ids preserve resume semantics; dry-run performs no workspace or journal write; CLI help/contracts describe the behavior; structured JSON and TOON recovery name the exact fix; packed consumer tests cover all migration kinds, repeated plans, explicit override, malformed input, and cross-workspace collision resistance.
In a fresh workspace, run schema rename-type, rename-field, or remap-status without --migration-id, including --dry-run; the command emits a raw internal assertion and refuses to plan.

SDK planning deterministically derives a stable idempotency key when omitted, explicit ids remain authoritative for resume, dry-run is side-effect-free, and invalid input returns the standard typed actionable error envelope.
The nominally optional migration id is de facto required and omission surfaces the raw string Schema migration migrationId must be non-empty, including for dry-run.
schema evolution SDK and CLI adapter
Agents cannot discover or self-correct the headline schema-evolution workflow from runtime contracts and structured errors.
